sections.h2: What makes Hallandale Beach different from other Broward County cities when you sell?
sections.html:
Hallandale Beach is a small, oddly shaped city on Broward County's southern edge, and its odd outline comes from a 1947 deal. The city history says a legislative approval let it annex land from Federal Highway east to the ocean, while the oceanfront north of Beach Boulevard went to Hollywood. The city's total area is 4.55 square miles, of which 4.21 is land.

The 2020 census counted 41,217 people and 17,573 households, according to the city. A small footprint with that many households means a seller is usually dealing with condos, townhomes and older single-family lots close together, so check which rules your own parcel falls under.

sections.h2: How did Hallandale Beach get here?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in the 1890s, many of them Scandinavian farmers, and the community grew tomatoes. Luther Halland, recruited by the railroad developer Henry Flagler, was the first postmaster, and the town took the Hallandale name from him. The railway reached Miami in 1896, the first school opened in 1904, and the area stayed part of Dade County until 1915.

Hallandale Beach milestones from the city's history page
YearEvent
1927Town of Hallandale created, the eighth municipality in Broward County
1947Reincorporated as a city, with the eastern annexation
1953Commission-City Manager form of government adopted
1978Golden Isles annexed
1996Community Redevelopment Agency created by ordinance
1999Name changed to Hallandale Beach

The 1926 hurricane struck Hallandale with estimated winds up to 150 miles per hour, and the city history calls it the most destructive storm in United States history up to that time. Hurricane Katrina made its first landfall in Hallandale Beach in August 2005. Older homes here have lived through that weather, so a buyer's inspector will often ask about roofs, windows and past claims.

sections.h2: What draws buyers and visitors to Hallandale Beach?
sections.html:
Gulfstream Park opened on February 1, 1939, and the city says it now houses a racetrack, a casino and the Village of Gulfstream shopping and entertainment complex, which cost its owners $1.2 billion. A second casino, The Big Easy, and a financial district with bank and brokerage offices are also named on the city's page.

  • Parks: Foster Park, OB Johnson Park, Peter Bluesten Park and the city beach parks on the oceanfront.
  • Marina: the City Marina opened on February 22, 2013.
  • Golden Isles: a waterfront community annexed in 1978 that has its own tennis center and park.

sections.h2: How do permits work in Hallandale Beach?
sections.html:
The city's Building Division uses two online systems. ePermitsOneStop is a joint city and Broward County site where applicants submit plans so City and County staff review at the same time, and HB Self-Service lets you pay fees, check a permit and schedule inspections. You can search the portal by address or parcel and see permit history without an account.

That history search is useful to a seller. Before listing, look up your own address, find permits that never reached a final inspection, and ask the Building Division how to close them. Unfinished work on a roof, windows, electrical or a balcony enclosure is the kind of item that comes up at a buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: Who is the tax authority for a Hallandale Beach house?
sections.html:
Broward County Records, Taxes and Treasury collects the bill and also supports the Value Adjustment Board, which hears disputes over exemptions, classifications and values. The Recording Office is at 115 S. Andrews Ave, Room 114, Fort Lauderdale, and the phone is 954-831-4000 or 3-1-1, open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The Value Adjustment Board has its own address at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale.

The statewide calendar applies. Value is set each January 1, owners file for exemptions by March 1, the appraiser mails the proposed tax notice in August, and a challenge goes to the clerk within 25 days of that notice. Bills arrive in November, and the state's early-payment discounts step down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and certificates are sold by June 1.

sections.h2: What exemption and cap rules matter to a Hallandale Beach homeowner?
sections.html:
• Homestead: the first $25,000 applies to all taxes, and a second layer up to $25,000 applies to assessed value above $50,000 for non-school taxes.
  • Save Our Homes: yearly assessed increases are held to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change, and the reset on sale is automatic.
  • Rental: homestead ends when the unit is rented out or stops being the permanent home.
  • Portability: the benefit can follow you to a new Florida homestead if you set it up within three years.

Because a sale ends the seller's cap, ask the Broward Property Appraiser how the parcel will be reassessed for the buyer, and plan around a higher bill for the new owner. A buyer's own estimate may differ sharply from your current bill.

sections.h2: What do closing costs include when you sell in Hallandale Beach?
sections.html:
Broward is a standard county for doc stamps: 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, paid to the clerk when the deed is recorded. The Miami-Dade rate and its surtax do not apply here. Both the seller and the buyer are liable, even if the contract assigns the cost to one side.

Recording is charged per page under section 28.24. If your property sits in a condominium or homeowners association, ask the association for its estoppel or payoff letter early, since those items can add days to a closing.

sections.h2: What if the Hallandale Beach house is occupied, inherited or behind on payments?
sections.html:
An occupied rental affects the timeline. Month-to-month tenancies end on 30 days' notice, and the landlord has a 3-day notice for unpaid rent. After a landlord wins a judgment, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice before putting the landlord in possession.

If the owner has died, small estates can sometimes use summary administration, which is open when the non-exempt estate is no more than $150,000 or the decedent has been dead over two years. Foreclosure sales follow 20 to 35 days after judgment. A closing agent or Florida attorney can tell you which of these applies.

faqs.q: Which county is Hallandale Beach in?
faqs.a: Broward County. The area belonged to Dade County until Broward was formed in 1915.

faqs.q: When did Hallandale become a city?
faqs.a: The town was created in 1927, and it was reincorporated as a city in 1947. The name changed to Hallandale Beach on August 27, 1999.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax in Broward County?
faqs.a: Yes, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, collected by the clerk at recording. The Miami-Dade rate does not apply in Broward.

faqs.q: How do I check my permit history?
faqs.a: Use the HB Self-Service portal and search by address, parcel number or inspection number. No account is needed to view finalized documents.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property value challenge?
faqs.a: Petitions go to the clerk within 25 days of the proposed tax notice, and the Broward Value Adjustment Board hears them. Call 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444 with questions.
